stops.note: law, right, combined with dicere (to say)
to judge, to declare the law, from ius (law) and dicere (to say)
stops.meaning: to judge, to declare the law

stops.note: carried into French for deciding a legal case
settled as the English word for a person who decides legal cases, or to form an opinion
stops.meaning: a person who decides legal cases, or to form an opinion

current_meaning: a public official who presides over court cases, or to form an opinion about something
